evidence.quoted_text:
"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: The `manager_restarted` predicate only requires two positive, differing manager PIDs and differing nonempty invocation IDs. It does not require the before/after manager snapshots to be from the same boot, even though boot IDs are available and used for the reboot snapshot pair. A guest reboot between the manager snapshots can therefore produce the same PID/invocation differences and be misreported as an isolated manager restart. Adding nonempty equal manager boot IDs is the smallest compatible correction while retaining the existing PID and invocation-ID checks.
